messages:
alex: heads up — noticed a cost/regression spike after we enabled multi-backend fanout for traces (Tempo + Honeycomb + Datadog). most expensive orgs are small but chatty. we need a routing/sampling plan before we open this up further. :money_with_wings:
priya: yeah saw that dashboard. rough breakdown: datadog ingest cost went up 3x from duplication, tempo storage also jumped due to full retention replicas. we should avoid naive fanout for all orgs.
jamie: agreed. two quick concerns: 1) duplication causing billing + storage explosion, 2) span attribute normalization — some backends expect `service.name` vs `svc` and we end up with fragmented views.
alex: proposal: per-tenant routing policy + central sampling layer. route all traces to tempo by default, then selectively fanout based on org config (console toggle or tiers). apply upstream dedupe/sampling before exporter fanout.
kevin: sounds good. we can implement a small proxy collector that: 1) canonicalizes attributes, 2) applies sampling rules (head/tail), 3) dedupes by trace-id+span-hash, then fans out. keeps exporters simple.
priya: +1. UX needs to allow: - toggle per-org backends - sampling rate override - retention override for honeycomb/tempo/Datadog - cost estimate preview (console)
jamie: technical nit: tail-based sampling needs storage window and can increase memory/latency. if we do tail sampling the proxy must be careful about decision_wait and observability. example otel tail config we tested locally: ```processors:
  tail_sampling:
    decision_wait: 5s
    policies:
      - name: high_value
        type: attribute
        parameters:
          attribute: user.subscription
          value: enterprise
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch, tail_sampling]
      exporters: [tempo, datadog]
```
kevin: point taken. maybe simpler approach for v1: head sampling + deterministic keep for tagged high-value traces, plus a lightweight buffer for short tail decisions (2-3s). avoids big memory footprint. also add async dedupe cache with TTL.
priya: on retention: tempo uses object store TTL; honeycomb has dataset TTL. we should expose per-org retention policy but enforce a max cap via a routing policy that drops or downsamples older traces destined for expensive backends.
ops-bot: alert: trace-exporter-latency spiking in us-east-1, correlated with fanout bursts (see #incidents).
alex: thanks ops-bot — that's the exact symptom. when burst -> exporters block and we queue which inflates memory and delays. we need backpressure handling: either backoff + degrade fanout or route to cheaper sink (s3 cold) temporarily.
jamie: also recommend normalizing span.name and attributes at ingest to reduce cardinality in honeycomb. we should publish a canonical mapping doc for exporters so vendor dashboards agree.
kevin: next steps I can spin up a minimal proxy PoC: head-sampler + attribute canonicalizer + dedupe cache + feature-flagged fanout. will run it behind a canary with 10% orgs. timeline: 1 week prototype, 2 weeks canary.
priya: I'll mock console UX for toggles and cost estimates. need a new endpoint in admin API to set org routing config (simple JSON blob).
alex: action items: kevin prototype, priya UX + API contract, jamie write canonical attribute mapping doc, ops add alert suppression for canary noise. canary rollout plan: 10% traffic -> monitor cost delta and latency -> expand.
jamie: sounds good. small request: add an exporter flag `drop_on_backpressure: true/false` so we can decide policy per backend.
kevin: will add that to PoC. also instrument exporter telemetry so we can attribute egress cost per org/back-end (token-level).
alex: great — let's sync end of week. :calendar: "+1" if you agree on the plan.
priya: +1
jamie: +1
kevin: +1
ops-bot: noted: scheduled a follow-up thread for next-wed sync (1761712223).
